notes.2: The most common incorrect answer was B. The equation on the question paper is: uMnO – + vH+ + wI– → xMn2+ + yH O + zI The correctly balanced equation is: 2MnO – + 16H+ + 10I– → 2Mn2+ + 8H O + 5I The value of v is 16. Candidates who chose answer B believed v to be 8. This would mean z is 2.5. It is stated in the question that u, v, w, x, y, and z are all whole numbers, so B is incorrect.
notes.7: The most common incorrect answer was C. Most candidates knew that ideal gases are assumed to have no intermolecular forces. There was uncertainty over whether ideal gas molecules are assumed to have no mass or no volume. No volume is correct.
notes.31: The most common incorrect answer was A. The nine products are: • chloroethane • 1,1-dichloroethane and 1,2-dichloroethane • 1,1,1-trichloroethane and 1,1,2-trichloroethane • 1,1,1,2-tetrachloroethane and 1,1,2,2-tetrachloroethane • pentachloroethane • hexachloroethane The choice of A by many candidates suggests that the products considered were chloroethane, ‘dichloroethane’, ‘trichloroethane’, ‘tetrachloroethane’, pentachloroethane and hexachloroethane only.
notes.32: The most common incorrect answer was A. From this we can deduce that many candidates were confident that Y does not have stereoisomers, but were less sure about X. After the addition of Br to 1-methylcyclohexene, product X shows cis/trans isomerism and has two chiral carbons at positions 1 and 2 in the ring. This gives a total of 2 + 2 = 4 stereoisomers.
notes.36: The most common incorrect answer was D. Many candidates also incorrectly chose A and C. Compound B is hydrolysed to give CH CO H and HOCH CH CO H, both of which have the empirical formula CH O. 3 2 2 2 2 2 Compounds B and C do undergo hydrolysis but they both produce two products with differing empirical formulae. Compound D cannot be hydrolysed by HCl(aq).
notes.40: The most common incorrect answer was C. Peaks M and M+2 are of equal height, so compound X is a bromine compound. The correct answer must be C or D. To deduce the number of carbon atoms in a compound the formula from 22.2.5 in the syllabus is required.100 ÷ (1.1 × 15) gives the answer 6.06, so there are six carbon atoms per molecule. This confirms the correct answer as D and not C.
notes.key_messages: Candidates who gave the best answers were concise and precise. The accurate use of chemical terminology remains crucial to remove ambiguity from responses. Candidates should be reminded to address ‘explain’ questions fully by stating facts or rules of thumb, and then showing how these combine to give reasons for chemical phenomena. This often requires a secure understanding of bonding and structure within molecules, in particular for organic species, linking structural feature to mechanistic probabilities.
notes.general_comments: General comments Questions 4, 5, 14, 17, 18, 20, 27, 29, 30 and 39 were found to be the easiest. Many candidates found questions 1, 12, 13, 22, 28, 35 and 38 to be particularly difficult. These are reviewed Comments on specific questions The most common incorrect answer was A. Option A cannot true. For example, if element Y is sodium and element X is chlorine, the atomic radius of the elements decreases across period 3. Option B is correct because the lowest possible value for the atomic number of element Y is 1 and X is 7, so the n=1 shell of element X must be full.
